programme: FOSL1 (AP-1/Fra-1) driving an MMP1/MMP2/MMP9/MMP13-CXCL8/IL6 transcriptional programme, together with ARHGAP35 (p190RhoGAP, which itself targets FOS) tuning Rho-GTPase/actin tone at endothelial junctions, and NR4A3, an ischemia-induced immediate-early nuclear receptor, upregulating the adhesion molecules VCAM1 and ICAM1 — a neurovascular-unit-activation and blood-brain-barrier-breakdown module, epigenetically reinforced by HDAC1, which has been shown directly to gate BBB permeability.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease this module runs chronically and at low grade: MMP-mediated degradation of basement-membrane/tight-junction proteins, endothelial activation, and HDAC1-dependent barrier permeability contribute to impaired clearance of neurotoxic species and sustained neuroinflammation — the vascular/BBB-dysfunction axis of AD pathogenesis.
role_in_b: In stroke the same cassette fires acutely and at high amplitude during ischemia-reperfusion: immediate-early induction of FOSL1 and NR4A3, MMP9-led basement-membrane proteolysis, and VCAM1/ICAM1-mediated leukocyte adhesion and transmigration drive the secondary inflammatory injury and oedema that follow the infarct.
shared_axis: Both diseases converge on the same neurovascular-unit/BBB-integrity checkpoint, expressed chronically in AD and acutely in stroke, through AP-1/Rho-GTPase-driven endothelial activation and MMP-mediated barrier proteolysis — a link directly evidenced by a paper reporting shared endothelial metabolic shifts across AD and stroke.
reasoning: HDAC1 is independently documented to control BBB permeability in an AD model and to be dysregulated in post-stroke neuroinflammation, and NR4A3 recurs across independent stroke hub-gene/expression studies, giving two of the four carrying factors solid within-disease anchors. But ARHGAP35 has no disease-specific literature here (only thyroid carcinoma), FOSL1's AD evidence is indirect, and no single retrieved paper states this four-factor module as a shared AD-stroke axis — so the cross-disease connection rests on one joint endothelial paper plus general neurovascular reasoning rather than being fully retrieved.
support: PMID 38329647 — HDAC1 directly shown to mediate BBB permeability in an in vitro AD model. PMID 37775708 — reports shared endothelial metabolic shifts across stroke and AD, the one paper tying the two diseases together on this vascular axis. PMID 41388741 — HDAC1 dysregulation drives pro-inflammatory microglial activation and worsens post-stroke neuroinflammation. PMID 42517197 — HDAC1-linked oxidative-stress modulation studied in a cerebral-ischemia model. PMID 40320842 — NR4A3 named among therapeutic targets for neuronal regeneration after ischemic stroke. PMID 34500302 — proteomic/transcriptomic study naming NR4A3 among transcription factors mediating post-stroke protection. PMID 39349220 — FOSL1 implicated in interleukin/inflammatory signalling in an AD neuroprotection study.
how_to_falsify: In a human brain-endothelial/pericyte BBB co-culture, apply Aβ oligomers (AD-mimic) and oxygen-glucose deprivation (stroke-mimic) separately, each with and without combined knockdown of FOSL1 and ARHGAP35 and with HDAC1 inhibition and NR4A3 knockdown as parallel arms. If transendothelial permeability, MMP9 activity, and VCAM1/ICAM1 induction rise equally regardless of these perturbations, the proposed module is not the operative driver of barrier breakdown in either condition.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|brain, which is literally the BBB interface, so a vascular-barrier axis is anatomically apt rather than a reach. Only 24 patient-group comparisons and 6 independent cohort pairs back these concordances — modest replication depth. TP73, the single highest-concordance factor overall (22/24), sits outside this module: its targets (MDM2, CDKN1A, GADD45A, MGMT, MLH1) are DNA-damage/apoptosis genes, not vascular ones, and its one AD paper reports a lack of association — so this account deliberately does not use the strongest recurring factor and is not a full explanation of everything concordant. ARHGAP35's only retrieved literature is in thyroid carcinoma, not brain or vascular tissue — its place here rests on its FOS target, not documented disease biology. Excluded tissue-generic factors (HLX, IRF1, STAT1, VDR, ERG, FOXO4, HDAC7, E2F1, SREBF2, PBX1, ZEB1) include several immune/interferon regulators; their removal means the generic immune/interferon layer common to blood and brain was stripped out by design, not shown absent from the biology. Single-view factors (STAT1, HLX, NRG1, VDR, ZMIZ1, NR3C1) topped only one patient group each and are excluded on that basis alone.
